clue.text: A hand-out mostly beats the blues

indicators.note: mostly means the word for the hand-out loses its final letter

parts.note: the dole is a state hand-out to the unemployed
drums means beats, as one beats a drum

explanation.surface: Getting a hand-out cheers you up more than anything when you are low.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' docks the last letter of DOLE, leaving DOL.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in the doldrums is a spell of low spirits, the same gloomy mood as having the blues.

clue.text: Orgy's beginning with fifty, approximately, imbibing old wine

indicators.note: beginning picks out the opening letter of the word Orgy's

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral for fifty

indicators.note: imbibing means the phrase for approximately takes in, or drinks, the letter for old

parts.note: or so means approximately

explanation.surface: Around fifty guests at the start of an orgy drink some vintage wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'imbibing' puts O inside ORSO to make OROSO.
explanation.definitionFit: Oloroso is a dark, rich style of sherry, a fortified Spanish wine.

clue.text: Inaction over club, say, currently being moved?

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece over another means it comes first

parts.note: drift is aimless inaction, letting things slide
a wood is a kind of golf club, so say marks an example

explanation.surface: Doing nothing over a golf club, perhaps while the current carries something along.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is cryptic: driftwood is timber carried along by water currents.
explanation.definitionFit: Driftwood is timber washed along by the sea or a river, so it is literally moved by a current.

clue.text: How to make a magazine free of charge

definitions.text: How to make a magazine free of charge

parts.words: How to make a magazine free of charge
parts.note: a gun's magazine holds the charge or cartridges; emptying it of them, not giving it away free, is what is meant

explanation.surface: Advice on running a magazine that readers get for nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Magazine' suggests a periodical and 'free of charge' a price; really it is a firearm's magazine being emptied of its charge.
explanation.definitionFit: To unload a gun is to remove its ammunition, leaving the magazine without a charge.

clue.text: Eton King's Scouts assembled to maintain position staunchly

indicators.note: assembled means the letters are put together in a new order

parts.note: the letters of King's are used, apostrophe dropped

explanation.surface: Eton's royal Scout troop gathers and stands firm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'assembled' rearranges ETON, KINGS and SCOUTS together.
explanation.definitionFit: To stick to one's guns is an idiom for refusing to back down on an opinion, holding one's ground firmly.

clue.text: Reversal of dogma is surprising, involving this country

indicators.note: Reversal of says the hidden letters are read backwards
involving means the words dogma is surprising contain the letters wanted

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Upending dogma is a surprising thing for this country to do.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft gave the definition as 'involving this country' with no hidden-word signal; 'involving' is that signal, the phrase containing AISSUR, which turned round gives the country.
explanation.definitionFit: Russia is the country the setter means, a nation spanning eastern Europe and northern Asia.

clue.text: Container the main body loot

parts.note: the ruck is the main body of a crowd or of runners in a race
to sack a town is to loot it

explanation.surface: A box holding the bulk of the stolen goods.
explanation.definitionFit: A rucksack is a bag carried on the back, a container for gear.

clue.text: Plant seen about in border

indicators.note: in says the word for about sits inside the word for border

parts.note: a skirt is a border or edge, as in the skirts of a town
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: A plant spotted somewhere along the edge of a flowerbed.
explanation.definitionFit: Skirret is a perennial plant grown for its sweet edible roots, an old garden vegetable.

clue.text: Dispute caused by bishop in two of Gray's works?

indicators.note: in places the bishop's letter between the two rearranged copies
two of means the rearranged name is used twice over
works suggests the poet's writings but means the name is worked into a new order

parts.note: the letters of Gray's are used, apostrophe dropped
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: A row stirred up by a bishop over a pair of Thomas Gray's poems.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests poems by Thomas Gray; 'works' is the anagram signal, 'two of' doubles the result and 'in' sets the bishop between the copies.
explanation.definitionFit: Argy-bargy is informal British for a noisy quarrel or squabble.

clue.text: Jolly little woman with not much bottle!

parts.note: Jo March is one of the sisters in Louisa May Alcott's novel Little Women
a vial is a small bottle

explanation.surface: A cheerful small lady who has hardly any courage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bottle' is British slang for courage, which the surface plays on; here it is a literal small bottle.
explanation.definitionFit: Jovial means cheerful and good-humoured, the same as jolly.

clue.text: Accruing from business in fashionable porcelain

indicators.note: in says the abbreviation for business goes inside the other two pieces

parts.note: in means fashionable, as in the in thing
Ming is fine Chinese porcelain of the Ming dynasty
Co is the abbreviation for company, a business

explanation.surface: Earnings coming from a firm dealing in trendy china.
explanation.definitionFit: Incoming money is money arriving or accruing, as in incoming funds.

clue.text: Frank takes the same position as Luke

parts.note: a post is a position, a job or a station
Mark, like Luke, is one of the four gospel writers, so he takes the same position

explanation.surface: Someone named Frank holds the same view as someone called Luke.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Frank' reads as a man's name but is the verb for stamping mail. 'takes the same position as Luke' points to another evangelist, Mark.
explanation.definitionFit: A postmark is the stamp that franks a letter, cancelling its postage.

clue.text: Old gem a sailor found on a craggy outcrop

indicators.note: in an across clue, found on means placed after the other piece

parts.note: a scar is a steep rocky outcrop or cliff
AB, able seaman, is a sailor

explanation.surface: An ancient jewel picked up by a seaman on a rocky headland.
explanation.definitionFit: A scarab was an ancient Egyptian gem carved in the shape of a dung beetle.

clue.text: Black employed in plant — a mechanical worker

indicators.note: employed in means the letter for black is put to work inside the word for plant

parts.note: to root is to plant, or a root is part of a plant
B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A Black man taken on at a factory as a machine operator.
explanation.definitionFit: A robot is a machine built to do work automatically, a mechanical labourer.

clue.text: State-recognized church publication used by cooks

parts.note: RI is Rhode Island, a US state
CE, the Church of England, is the established or state-recognized church
a paper is a publication, a newspaper

explanation.surface: A newsletter of the established church, used in kitchens.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a description: rice paper is the edible sheet bakers put under macaroons.
explanation.definitionFit: Rice paper is edible wafer sheeting that bakers and confectioners lay under biscuits and sweets.

clue.text: Bird returning to gnarled trees in a cathedral city

indicators.note: returning means the bird's name is read backwards

parts.note: a crow is a bird

indicators.note: gnarled means twisted, so the letters of trees are twisted into a new order

explanation.surface: A bird flies back to some twisted trees in a city with a cathedral.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returning' turns CROW to WORC; 'gnarled' rearranges TREES to ESTER.
explanation.definitionFit: Worcester is an English city in the West Midlands famous for its medieval cathedral.

clue.text: The present way thus to circumvent this jolly weather

indicators.note: circumvent means go round, so the outer pieces surround the inner ones

parts.note: so means thus
now is the present moment
St, street, is a way
a jolly is old naval slang for a Royal Marine, abbreviated RM

explanation.surface: Here and now, a way to get round this jolly bad weather.
explanation.walkthrough: 'circumvent' wraps the outer pair round the inner pair. A jolly is old naval slang for a Royal Marine, and 'jolly weather' falsely suggests a cheerful day.
explanation.definitionFit: A snowstorm is a spell of weather with heavy snowfall and wind.

clue.text: Lack of order is the prelude to raising endless din

indicators.note: the prelude to means these pieces come before the next

parts.note: OM is the Order of Merit

indicators.note: in a down clue raising means the letters are read upwards, backwards
endless means the word for din loses its last letter

parts.note: noise means din

explanation.surface: Missing an order is the start of an uproar that never stops.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' cuts NOISE to NOIS and 'raising' turns it to SION.
explanation.definitionFit: An omission is something left out, so a gap or lack.

clue.text: Cook mince — don't put sauce in -

indicators.note: cook means the letters are cooked up into a new arrangement

parts.note: the letters of don't are used, apostrophe dropped

explanation.surface: A recipe step: cook the mince, but leave out the sauce.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cook' rearranges MINCE and DONT.
explanation.definitionFit: A condiment is a relish or seasoning added to food, such as a sauce.

clue.text: Cipher is a matter of no importance

definitions.meaning: a cipher is a zero, the figure 0
something trivial that does not count

explanation.definitionFit: A cipher is a zero, a figure worth naught, and a trifle of no consequence is called a mere naught too.

clue.text: A cottage for two at the close of day

parts.note: both means the two together

indicators.note: at the close of picks out the final letter of day

explanation.surface: A small house for a couple to retire to at the end of the day.
explanation.walkthrough: A bothy is a Scottish word for a basic hut or cottage.
explanation.definitionFit: A bothy is a simple hut or cottage in Scotland, often a shelter for walkers or farm workers.

clue.text: One who'd turned out for a dance

indicators.note: turned out means the letters are turned into a new order

parts.note: the letters of who'd are used, apostrophe dropped

explanation.surface: Someone who showed up for a dance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned out' rearranges ONE and WHOD.
explanation.definitionFit: A hoedown is a lively American folk dance or the social gathering held for one.

clue.text: Showing no trace of a brogue, perhaps

definitions.text: Showing no trace of a brogue, perhaps

parts.words: Showing no trace of a brogue, perhaps
parts.note: a brogue looks like an Irish accent but is a sturdy shoe, so this describes feet with no shoes on

explanation.surface: Someone speaking without any hint of an Irish accent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brogue' means both a lilting accent and a heavy leather shoe; the shoe sense is the one wanted.
explanation.definitionFit: Unshod means barefoot, wearing no shoes such as brogues.

clue.text: Quiet musketeer's quality that excites sadness

parts.note: p, piano, is the musical direction for quiet
Athos is one of Dumas's three musketeers

explanation.surface: A gentle musketeer has a melancholy air about him.
explanation.definitionFit: Pathos is the quality in art or life that arouses pity and sorrow.

clue.text: Rock is inside on the left

indicators.note: inside means is goes within the word for rock

parts.note: sinter is a rock, a deposit formed around hot springs

explanation.surface: Rock music is in, on the left side of the stage.
explanation.walkthrough: Sinter is a mineral deposit from hot springs. Sinister is Latin for left, used in heraldry.
explanation.definitionFit: Sinister in heraldry means the left-hand side of a shield, from the bearer's view.

clue.text: Collect from this desk?

parts.note: a collect is a short prayer in church, not a pick-up; the desk is one for praying at

explanation.surface: A notice telling you where to pick up your parcel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Collect' reads as a verb but is the noun for a short liturgical prayer, said from a kneeling desk.
explanation.definitionFit: A prie-dieu is a kneeling desk for prayer, from which a collect might be said.

clue.text: American poet who, they say, was first to get the bird

indicators.note: was first says the sounded word comes before the poet
they say means the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: the word who is said aloud
Edgar Allan Poe was an American poet

explanation.surface: An American poet who, so the story goes, was first to catch the bird.
explanation.walkthrough: WHO sounds like HOO.
explanation.definitionFit: The hoopoe is a crested bird with pinkish plumage and a distinctive hoo-hoo call.

clue.text: A man no one backed in this sphere of activity

parts.note: Reg is a man's name, short for Reginald

indicators.note: backed means the words no and one are read backwards

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A man no one supported in this field.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backed' turns NO + I into ION.
explanation.definitionFit: A region is an area or field, as in the region of science.

clue.text: Grounds for having a little cash transmitted to the borders

indicators.note: to the borders means the word for transmitted sits around the coin's word

parts.note: sent means transmitted
a dime is a US ten-cent coin, a little cash

explanation.surface: A reason to send a small sum of money out to the frontier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grounds' reads as reasons but means dregs such as coffee grounds.
explanation.definitionFit: Sediment is matter that settles at the bottom, like coffee grounds.
